blocks.text: Intro
Immediate Downbeat | No Fade

92 BPM. Dry kick hits immediately with a crisp snare backbeat; rimshot answers. Tight closed hi-hat ticks evenly. A short vinyl drag strains against the beat, then releases. Warm plucked bass enters after two bars. No melodic intro.

Yeah.
Hold up.
Brief drop: hi-hat alone.
Slow the clock.
Verse 1
Close-Miked Talk-Rap | Slightly Behind the Beat

Drums stay stubborn and exact. Bass repeats a two-note figure, sometimes anticipating beat one. Dusty electric piano drops one clipped chord between lines. Vocal is conversational, sharp, a little amused; never shouted.

Tap the glass. Don’t wait. Don’t stall.
Impulse talking loud — guess it makes the call.

Clock leans hard on every second.
Truth gets sold as repetition.
Bass and piano cut. Two isolated rim clicks mark the words.

Tick. Tick.
Push ahead.
Stillness labeled
“Probably dead.”
Pre-Chorus 1
Dry, Almost Doctrinal
Snare becomes rim clicks; bass hangs on one repeated note. Muted trumpet answers with two short descending notes. Leave the vocal completely exposed.

They call it wisdom when it fills these rooms.
They call it fate when it sets our tune.

But speed ain’t truth
Just ’cause it moves.
DJ cut — a brief dragged and chopped “slow the clock”; groove snaps back on time.
Chorus 1
Create Space, Don't Slow Down
Drums thin to kick, snare and half-time hat. Bass disappears for the first command. No horns; electric piano offers only isolated answers. Let the gaps between words be audible.

Slow. The clock.
When it turns on us.
Bass returns only after “us.”

Hold. The breath.
Before the rush.
One-bar drum-only pocket; no fill.

Slow it down.
Hold the room.
Two dry piano chords; one low muted-trumpet reply.
Let attention choose the tune.
Verse 2
Deeper Pocket | A Little More Bite

Same tempo and volume. Bass develops playful syncopated steps around the rigid kick. Add soft snare ghost notes, never a busy fill. Piano grows more percussive. Muted trumpet punctuates only the ends of selected lines. Vocal sounds wrier, not angrier.

Noise dressed up as meaning.
Busy people “deeply thinking.”

Fairness measured edge to edge
Like the scale ain’t already bent.

With tilted ground
Before the race

Silence helps
Keep it that way.
Pre-Chorus 2
Cold Restraint
Piano and brass vanish. Bass repeats one note. Kick remains steady; the snare feels stark because everything else has stepped aside.

Strength gets framed
As feeling less.

That lie still
Passed our tests.
Turntable catches a fraction of the beat, releases it precisely on the downbeat.
Chorus 2
More Air, Heavier Meaning
Same stripped chorus groove. Bass speaks only in the spaces between lines. One uneasy electric-piano chord on “consume”; one trumpet note after “room.” No extra vocal layers.

Slow. The clock.
When it turns on us.

Hold. The breath.
Before the rush.

There’s a space
They can't consume
When attention reads the room.
Final Chorus
Exposed, Not Bigger
First two lines: bass and rim clicks only, with faint hi-hat counting time. Kick and snare return beneath “If we punish,” then peel away. Let “away” hang almost alone. No crescendo.

Slow. The clock.
When it turns on us.

If we punish naïveté
We starve our wonder away.
Outro
Spoken | Dismantle the Groove
Kick and bass return quietly. Bass drops out at “hollow.” Snare stops at “voices.” Hi-hat keeps ticking beneath the final words.
When we survive into something hollow—
Name the voices we chose to follow.
One short record-stop scrape. Hard cut. No reverb tail.

notebook.style: 92 BPM boom-bap: old-school rhythmic DNA, lean modern mix, late-night jazz-rap color, Drums dry and unwavering: punchy kick, crisp snare, spare rimshots, tight eighth-note hat, quiet ghost notes, slight swing, no tempo shifts, Round plucked bass repeats a stubborn two-note motif, then grows slyly syncopated in verse 2, Dusty electric piano adds clipped low chord replies, no pads, Muted trumpet offers rare one- or two-note comments, not a horn section, Turntable scratches interrupt deliberately: short drag, cut, release; underlying pulse never flinches, Solo close-miked talk-rap: human grain, dry wit, clear consonants, slightly behind the beat, restrained authority; never shouted or belted, Chorus arrangements subtract bass, keys, and hats to create audible air; pauses carry the hook, Final chorus should feel exposed, not bigger, Outro dismantles groove one instrument at a time and stops hard, No synth washes, risers, glossy layers, backing vocals or dramatic climax
